correctness.rationale: For irreducible cubic A, trace and rank exclude all nonzero traces: tripotent T must have trace 0 or 1, and in the trace-one cases either rankT=1 or T+I square-zero, contradicting invertibility of A or A+I. In the trace-zero case the sole possible tripotent characteristic polynomial is X^3+X. The rank-one determinant lemma together with the cyclic basis (u,Au,A^2u) uniquely constructs and exhausts all square-zero N=uv with that polynomial; Cayley-Hamilton proves tripotency. The finite Singer centralizer action follows from K[A]=F_(q^3). Exhaustive GF2 and GF4 code checks passed but are not used as an infinite proof.

originality.rationale: An exact projective-plane classification of every tripotent-plus-square-zero decomposition for an irreducible cubic over any characteristic-two field, with Singer-torsor symmetry over finite fields, goes beyond the known nonderogatory square-zero existence theorem (arXiv:2403.15138v1), diagonalizable-plus-square-zero constructions (arXiv:2604.15286v1), and the later binary existence/nonexistence criterion (arXiv:2611.24594v1). Actual searches of prior published mathematical records found related but different fiber counts. A historical implicit corollary remains possible.
